entities.name: Esophageal perforation
observations: Post-esophageal instrumentation chest pain, dyspnea, and supraclavicular crepitus are highly concerning for iatrogenic esophageal perforation.
In hemodynamically stable patients, contrast-enhanced CT of the neck/chest/upper abdomen with water-soluble oral contrast when feasible is a contemporary informative initial study.
Plain radiography may show indirect signs but does not reliably exclude perforation.

entities.name: CT for stable perforation
observations: For suspected esophageal perforation in a stable patient, CT with intravenous contrast, supplemented by water-soluble oral contrast if safe, evaluates the leak and mediastinal or pleural contamination.

entities.name: Water-soluble esophagram sequence
observations: Traditional evaluation begins with chest/neck radiographs, followed by a water-soluble Gastrografin esophagram when the patient can swallow; thin barium may follow a negative study if suspicion remains high.
Current practice may proceed directly to CT in stable patients, while radiographs alone should not delay definitive imaging.

entities.name: PMID:25428920
observations: Prospective cohort of 300 therapy-naive HIV-1-positive adults starting first-line ART in rural Cameroon, followed for 12 months.
Among 238 participants with Month-12 viral-load data, 38 (16%) had virological failure defined as HIV RNA ≥1000 copies/mL.
Baseline minority drug-resistance mutations detected by next-generation sequencing occurred in 6/30 (20%) failures versus 6/35 (17%) matched controls; P=0.77.

Lower baseline CD4 count and poorer adherence, especially interruptions from ART unavailability, were associated with virological failure; the authors concluded failure was not associated with baseline minority resistance.
At Month 12, 63% of patients with virological failure had at least one drug-resistance mutation; common mutations included M184V and K103N.

entities.name: HIV-1 infection
observations: The study evaluated treatment-naive adults with HIV-1 infection initiating first-line ART in rural Cameroon.

entities.name: Minority resistance not predictive
observations: In rural Cameroon, baseline minority HIV drug resistance was not statistically associated with virological failure after 12 months of first-line ART: 20% of failures versus 17% of matched controls, P=0.77.
The study instead identified lower baseline CD4 count and poorer adherence as associated with failure.
